answer: Before Tokyo, Kyoto was Japan's capital. Emperor Kanmu founded it in 794 as Heian-kyō, and it stayed the imperial capital for more than a thousand years [1][2]. The Emperor and the central government moved to Tokyo (then called Edo) during the Meiji Restoration, in 1868–1869 [2][3]. Before Kyoto, the capital moved several times, most notably to Nara (Heijō-kyō) from 710 to 784, and briefly to Nagaoka-kyō [1].
